claim: Sedimentary rocks host a vast reservoir of organic carbon, including 2-methylhopane biomarkers.
source: Sedimentary rocks host a vast reservoir of organic carbon, such as 2-methylhopane biomarkers, whose evolutionary significance we poorly understand.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a general scientific fact about sedimentary rocks.

claim: Hopanoid 2-methylation specifically renders native bacterial membranes more rigid at concentrations that are relevant in vivo.
source: Fluorescence polarization studies of small unilamellar vesicles revealed that hopanoid 2-methylation specifically renders native bacterial membranes more rigid at concentrations that are relevant in vivo.
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization experiments described in the manuscript.

claim: Cholesterol plays diverse roles in maintaining membrane structural integrity, modifying membrane rigidity, serving as a biosynthetic precursor for steroid hormones, vitamin D, and bile acids, or acting as a protein modifier for signaling pathways.
source: This essential sterol plays diverse roles in maintaining membrane structural integrity, modifying membrane rigidity, serving as a biosynthetic precursor for steroid hormones, vitamin D, and bile acids, or acting as a protein modifier for signaling pathways (Hanukoglu, 1992; Gallet, 2011; Song et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Hopanoid molecular fossils date back over a billion years.
source: For example, hopanoid molecular fossils, 'hopanes', date back over a billion years (Brocks et al., 2005)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Brocks et al., 2005.

claim: The global stock of hopanoids that can be extracted from sedimentary rocks is estimated to be 10^13 or 10^14 tons.
source: the global stock of hopanoids that can be extracted from sedimentary rocks is estimated to be 1013 or 1014 tons, more than the estimated 1012 tons of organic carbon in all living organisms (Ourisson et al., 1984).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Ourisson et al., 1984.

claim: Hopanoids are thought to be sterol surrogates in bacteria.
source: In contrast to steroids, hopanoids are a less well studied but evolutionarily significant and chemically diverse class of lipids that are thought to be sterol surrogates in bacteria (Figure 1) (Rohmer et al., 1979; Ourisson et al., 1987).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Rohmer et al., 1979 and Ourisson et al., 1987.

claim: Hopanoids promote resistance to antibiotics, detergents, extreme pH, and high osmolarity.
source: For example, studies using hopanoid-deficient mutants have shown that hopanoids promote resistance to antibiotics, detergents, extreme pH, and high osmolarity (Welander et al., 2009; Sáenz, 2010; Schmerk et al., 2011; Malott et al., 2012; Kulkarni et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior studies.

claim: Bacteriohopanetetrol cyclitol ether can condense membranes at high temperatures but fluidize membranes at low temperatures.
source: Biophysical studies using mixtures of hopanoids and model lipids have demonstrated that, like cholesterol, bacteriohopanetetrol cyclitol ether can condense membranes at high temperatures but fluidize membranes at low temperatures (Poralla et al., 1980).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Poralla et al., 1980.

claim: Bacteriohopanetetrol (BHT) and bacteriohopanemonol can condense model membranes.
source: Similarly, bacteriohopanetetrol (BHT) and bacteriohopanemonol can condense model membranes, and diplopterol (Dip) can form liquid ordered microdomains (Kannenberg et al., 1983; Nagumo et al., 1991; Ourisson and Rohmer, 1992; Sáenz et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: Diplopterol (Dip) can form liquid ordered microdomains.
source: Similarly, bacteriohopanetetrol (BHT) and bacteriohopanemonol can condense model membranes, and diplopterol (Dip) can form liquid ordered microdomains (Kannenberg et al., 1983; Nagumo et al., 1991; Ourisson and Rohmer, 1992; Sáenz et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: Methylation of C-2 on the A-ring of hopanoids is preserved episodically in ancient sedimentary rocks dating back to 1.6 billion years ago.
source: Among various hopanoid modifications, methylation of C-2 on the A-ring has drawn attention from Earth scientists because this modification is preserved episodically in ancient sedimentary rocks dating back to 1.6 billion years ago
evidence: This claim is stated in the introduction and is based on geological evidence.

claim: Spikes in the C30 2Me-hopane index through geologic time are correlated with episodes of oceanic anoxic events (OAEs).
source: Intriguingly, spikes in the C30 2Me-hopane index (ratio of methylated short hopanes to total short hopanes) through geologic time are correlated with episodes of oceanic anoxic events (OAEs), which are thought to have imposed heightened stress on the biosphere (Knoll et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Knoll et al., 2007.

claim: At 25°C, the Δshc mutant, which lacks all hopanoids, had the least rigid membrane.
source: At 25°C, the Δshc mutant, which lacks all hopanoids, had the least rigid membrane.
evidence: This claim is supported by whole cell membrane rigidity measurements shown in Figure 2.

claim: The production of only short-chain hopanoids (ΔhpnH) is sufficient to recover the rigidity level close to that of the WT.
source: Interestingly, the production of only short-chain hopanoids (ΔhpnH) is sufficient to recover the rigidity level close to that of the WT.
evidence: This claim is supported by whole cell membrane rigidity measurements shown in Figure 2.

claim: When an adenosine molecule is attached to short hopanoids and accumulates in the ΔhpnG mutant, rigidity decreases to Δshc levels.
source: However, when an adenosine molecule is attached to short hopanoids and accumulates in the ΔhpnG mutant, rigidity decreases to Δshc levels.
evidence: This claim is supported by whole cell membrane rigidity measurements shown in Figure 2.

claim: In ΔhpnN where hopanoids are unable to be transported to the outer membrane, membrane rigidity is similar to ΔhpnG.
source: Furthermore, in ΔhpnN where hopanoids are unable to be transported to the outer membrane (Doughty et al., 2011), membrane rigidity is similar to ΔhpnG.
evidence: This claim is supported by whole cell membrane rigidity measurements shown in Figure 2 and a citation to Doughty et al., 2011.

claim: The hydrophobic reporter dye diphenyl hexatriene (DPH) reflects mostly the rigidity of the outer membrane.
source: First, the hydrophobic reporter dye we used for fluorescence polarization measurements, diphenyl hexatriene (DPH), reflects mostly the rigidity of the outer membrane.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental results with different mutants.

claim: The types of hopanoids and their respective localization between the inner and outer membranes directly impact membrane rigidity.
source: Second, the types of hopanoids and their respective localization between the inner and outer membranes directly impact membrane rigidity.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental results with different mutants.

claim: No obvious impact on rigidity was found in the absence of either bacteriohopane aminotriol (ΔhpnO) or 2-methylhopanoid (ΔhpnP) or both (ΔhpnOP) compared to WT.
source: Interestingly, no obvious impact on rigidity was found in the absence of either bacteriohopane aminotriol (ΔhpnO) or 2-methylhopanoid (ΔhpnP) or both (ΔhpnOP) compared to WT (Figure 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by whole cell membrane rigidity measurements shown in Figure 2.

claim: The total yield of the fractionated membranes was about 10% weight of dried cells.
source: Table 2 shows that the total yield of the fractionated membranes was about 10% weight of dried cells, which is comparable to 9.1% in Escherichia coli (Neidhardt and Curtiss, 1996).
evidence: This claim is supported by data in Table 2 and compared to a cited value for E. coli.

claim: The yields of the total lipid extract (TLE) from the lyophilized fractionated membranes were ∼12–15% from the IM and ∼5% for the OM.
source: The yields of the total lipid extract (TLE) from the lyophilized fractionated membranes were ∼12–15% from the IM and ∼5% for the OM.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental measurements of lipid extraction yields.

claim: In both WT and ΔhpnP, each type of hopanoid is enriched in the OM compared to the IM.
source: In both WT and ΔhpnP, each type of hopanoid is enriched in the OM compared to the IM.
evidence: This claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 4.

claim: The total of (2Me)-Dip and (2Me)-BHT in the IM is ∼2.6 mol% of TLE, whereas in the OM, the value can reach 8–11 mol%.
source: The total of these four hopanoids in the IM is ∼2.6 mol% of TLE, whereas in the OM, the value can reach 8–11 mol%.
evidence: This claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 4.

claim: For individual hopanoids in WT, the mol% in IM and OM are 1% and 2% for Dip, 1% and 2.4% for 2Me-Dip, 0.4% and 3.4% for BHT, and 0.1% and 0.3% for 2Me-BHT, respectively.
source: For individual hopanoids in WT, the mol% in IM and OM are 1% and 2% for Dip, 1% and 2.4% for 2Me-Dip, 0.4% and 3.4% for BHT, and 0.1% and 0.3% for 2Me-BHT, respectively.
evidence: This claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 4.

claim: In ΔhpnP, the IM and OM values are 2% and 7.5% for Dip, and 0.5% and 4.3% for BHT, respectively.
source: In ΔhpnP, the IM and OM values are 2% and 7.5% for Dip, and 0.5% and 4.3% for BHT, respectively (Figure 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 4.

claim: The ratio of total hopanoids in the OM vs IM is 3.1 ± 0.4 and 4.4 ± 0.6 for WT and ΔhpnP, respectively, which is a significant difference (p = 0.038).
source: The ratio of total hopanoids in the OM vs IM is 3.1 ± 0.4 and 4.4 ± 0.6 for WT and ΔhpnP, respectively, which is a significant difference (p = 0.038).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantification data and statistical analysis.

claim: Long-chain hopanoids are enriched in the OM compared to the IM in both WT and ΔhpnP.
source: Comparing the ratios between short ((2Me)-Dip) and long ((2Me)-BHT) chain hopanoids revealed an enrichment of long-chain hopanoids in the OM compared to the IM in both WT and ΔhpnP (Figure 5).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 5.

claim: About equal amounts of 2Me-Dip and Dip were found in both IM and OM.
source: Interestingly, about equal amounts of 2Me-Dip and Dip were found in both IM and OM
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 5.

claim: 2Me-BHT is 16% and 8% of BHT in the IM and OM, respectively.
source: whereas 2Me-BHT is 16% and 8% of BHT in the IM and OM, respectively
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Hopanoid 2-methylation has neither strong nor consistent effects on the partitioning of short and long species between the IM and OM.
source: suggesting hopanoid 2-methylation has neither strong nor consistent effects on the partitioning of short and long species between the IM and OM (Figure 5).
evidence: This is inferred from the data shown in Figure 5.

claim: 2-methylation impacts the total amount of hopanoid enrichment in the OM.
source: However, our data do indicate that 2-methylation impacts that total amount of hopanoid enrichment in the OM.
evidence: This is inferred from the data comparing WT and ΔhpnP.

claim: The addition of cholesterol increases membrane rigidity in DOPC vesicles in a concentration-dependent manner.
source: Starting with the simplest single lipid background, DOPC, the addition of cholesterol increases membrane rigidity and the magnitude of change is proportional to the amounts of cholesterol added (black line, Figure 6A).
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The addition of squalene makes DOPC membranes less rigid in a concentration-dependent fashion.
source: Interestingly, the addition of the hopanoid precursor, squalene, has the opposite effect as cholesterol and makes the membrane less rigid in a concentration-dependent fashion (magenta line, Figure 6A).
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: When Dip is added to DOPC, the membrane rigidity is unaffected.
source: However, when Dip is added, the membrane rigidity is unaffected (blue line, Figure 6A).
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: When Dip is processed to produce BHT, it rigidifies DOPC vesicles in the same manner as cholesterol.
source: However, when Dip is further processed by the cell to produce BHT, it rigidifies DOPC vesicles in the same manner as cholesterol (red line, Figure 6A).
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: 2-methylation of both Dip and BHT has striking effects on their ability to rigidify DOPC.
source: 2-methylation of both Dip and BHT has striking effects on their ability to rigidify DOPC.
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: At 20 mol%, 2Me-Dip outperforms cholesterol and BHT in rigidifying DOPC membranes.
source: Not only does 2-methylation increase DOPC membrane rigidity, but at 20 mol%, 2Me-Dip even outperforms cholesterol and BHT (cyan line, Figure 6A).
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: 2Me-BHT increases DOPC membrane rigidity similar to cholesterol, though the difference from BHT is much smaller than that between Dip and 2Me-Dip.
source: 2Me-BHT also increases membrane rigidity similar to cholesterol, even though the difference from BHT is much smaller than that between Dip and 2Me-Dip (orange line, Figure 6A).
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Methylation itself changes the biophysical properties of hopanoids, which directly impacts membrane fluidity.
source: This result demonstrates methylation itself changes the biophysical properties of hopanoids, which directly impacts membrane fluidity.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental results showing differential effects of methylated vs. non-methylated hopanoids.

claim: E. coli PLE SUVs are more rigid than DOPC SUVs.
source: Compared to DOPC alone, the SUVs from E. coli PLE are more rigid, probably because the difference in fatty acid chain saturation (green square, Figure 6A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization data shown in Figure 6.

claim: Dip has a small rigidifying effect in the E. coli PLE background, with no concentration dependence.
source: Unlike in DOPC, Dip has a small rigidifying effect in the E. coli PLE background, yet similar to DOPC, no concentration dependence is observed (blue line, Figure 6B).
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: 2Me-Dip rigidifies E. coli PLE but shows lower capacity to rigidify the membrane than cholesterol.
source: Addition of 2Me-Dip also rigidifies E. coli PLE, but in contrast to what was observed for DOPC, 2Me-Dip shows lower capacity to rigidify the membrane than cholesterol (cyan line, Figure 6B).
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: BHT rigidifies E. coli PLE membranes but seems to saturate at 10 mol%.
source: Interestingly, the extended hopanoid, BHT, also rigidifies the membrane, but seemed to saturate at 10 mol% (red line, Figure 6B).
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: 2Me-BHT strongly rigidifies E. coli PLE membranes and has a concentration dependence.
source: Surprisingly, in sharp contrast to the DOPC background, 2Me-BHT strongly rigidifies the E. coli PLE membranes and has a concentration dependence (orange line, Figure 6B).
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The impact of 2-methylation and hopanoid extension on membrane biophysical properties depends on the specific lipid environment.
source: This result shows that the impact of 2-methylation and hopanoid extension on a membrane biophysical property depends on the specific lipid environment.
evidence: This is inferred from comparing the effects in DOPC vs. E. coli PLE backgrounds.

claim: A total of 33 major phospholipids were identified in R. palustris TIE-1, including 10 PC, 9 PE, 7 PG, and 7 CL.
source: A total of 33 major phospholipids were identified, including 10 PC, 9 PE, 7 PG, and 7 CL (Table 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by LC-MS analysis data shown in Table 3.

claim: The IM in WT and ΔhpnP has ∼50%, ∼36%, and ∼12–14% of PC, PE, and PG, respectively.
source: Among the identified phospholipids, the IM in WT and ΔhpnP has ∼50%, ∼36%, and ∼12–14% of PC, PE, and PG, respectively
evidence: This claim is supported by LC-MS analysis data shown in Table 4.

claim: The OM in WT and ΔhpnP has ∼56–58%, ∼30–33%, and ∼11–12% of PC, PE, and PG, respectively.
source: whereas the OM in WT and ΔhpnP has ∼56–58%, ∼30–33%, and ∼11–12% of PC, PE, and PG, respectively.
evidence: This claim is supported by LC-MS analysis data shown in Table 4.

claim: The total identified phospholipid amount accounts for ∼26–34 wt% of the original TLE samples.
source: However, when we calculate the total identified phospholipid amount, it only accounts for ∼26–34 wt% of the original TLE samples (Table 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by LC-MS analysis data shown in Table 4.

claim: In both WT and ΔhpnP, the OM showed higher membrane rigidity than IM.
source: In both WT and ΔhpnP, the OM showed higher membrane rigidity than IM, which could be due to the higher hopanoid content in the OM (Figure 4) and differences in phospholipid content.
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization data shown in Figure 8.

claim: Compared to WT, the ΔhpnP IM and OM showed decreased rigidity.
source: Compared to WT, the ΔhpnP IM and OM showed decreased rigidity.
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization data shown in Figure 8.

claim: The addition of Dip has no effect on membrane rigidity in both the IM and OM of R. palustris TIE-1.
source: Similar to our observations in model lipids, the addition of Dip has no effect on membrane rigidity, both in the IM and OM.
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization data shown in Figure 8.

claim: 2Me-Dip rigidifies both IM and OM in a concentration-dependent manner.
source: However, 2Me-Dip rigidifies both IM and OM in a concentration-dependent manner, as seen in the model lipid SUVs.
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization data shown in Figure 8.

claim: BHT does not rigidify either the IM or OM of R. palustris TIE-1.
source: Interestingly, unlike the effects BHT exerts in model lipids, it does not rigidify either the IM or OM.
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization data shown in Figure 8.

claim: 2Me-BHT rigidifies both the IM and OM of R. palustris TIE-1.
source: When BHT is methylated, it rigidifies both the IM and OM.
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization data shown in Figure 8.

claim: In the IM, the more 2Me-BHT present, the higher the membrane rigidity.
source: However, different trends can be seen between these membranes: in the IM, the more 2Me-BHT present, the higher the membrane rigidity
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization data shown in Figure 8.

claim: OM membrane rigidity appears to saturate by 5 mol% 2Me-BHT and remains constant between 5–20 mol% of 2Me-BHT.
source: yet OM membrane rigidity appears to saturate by 5 mol% 2Me-BHT and remains constant between 5–20 mol% of 2Me-BHT (Figure 8B).
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization data shown in Figure 8B.

claim: 2Me-hopanoids are enriched in the outer membrane of akinetes, survival cell types of the cyanobacterium Nostoc punctiforme.
source: (1) 2Me-hopanoids are enriched in the outer membrane of akinetes, survival cell types of the cyanobacterium Nostoc punctiforme (Doughty et al., 2009)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Doughty et al., 2009.

claim: A stress-responsive pathway upregulates the HpnP methylase in R. palustris.
source: (2) a stress-responsive pathway upregulates the HpnP methylase in R. palusris (Kulkarni et al., 2013)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Kulkarni et al., 2013.

claim: In modern environments, the capacity for 2Me-hopanoid production significantly correlates with organisms, metabolisms (e.g., nitrogen fixation), and environments that support plant–microbe interactions.
source: (3) in modern environments, the capacity for 2Me-hopanoid production significantly correlates with organisms, metabolisms (e.g., nitrogen fixation), and environments that support plant–microbe interactions (Ricci et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Ricci et al., 2014.

claim: (2Me)-hopanoids promote symbiosis.
source: This correlation, together with the observation that (2Me)-hopanoids promote symbiosis (Silipo et al., 2014)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Silipo et al., 2014.

claim: 2Me-hopanoids may indirectly facilitate nitrogen fixation by enhancing bacterial survival under the stressful conditions that accompany the establishment of symbiosis.
source: tempt us to speculate that 2Me-hopanoids may indirectly facilitate nitrogen fixation by enhancing bacterial survival under the stressful conditions that accompany the establishment of symbiosis (Gibson et al., 2008).
evidence: This is presented as speculation based on correlations and cited literature.

claim: Spikes in the 2Me-hopane index may reflect episodes of particular environmental stresses favoring the growth of organisms capable of withstanding it using (2Me)-hopanoids.
source: if correct, such an interpretation would indicate that spikes in the 2Me-hopane index may reflect episodes of particular environmental stresses favoring the growth of organisms capable of withstanding it using (2Me)-hopanoids.
evidence: This is presented as a speculative interpretation based on the findings.

claim: The addition or removal of methyl groups over the evolution of the cholesterol lipid family is thought to have optimally tuned cholesterol's ability to order or condense phospholipid membranes.
source: The addition or removal of methyl groups over the evolution of the cholesterol lipid family is thought to have optimally tuned cholesterol's ability to order or condense phospholipid membranes (Miao et al., 2002; Rog et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: When a methyl group is added onto the 2′ position of A-ring in hopanoid, the stearic hindrance between the 2-methyl group and the methyl groups at the 4′ and 10′ position of the A-ring could transform the ring from a chair to a twisted conformation.
source: We suggest that when a methyl group is added onto the 2′ position of A-ring in hopanoid, the stearic hindrance between the 2-methyl group and the methyl groups at the 4′ and 10′ position of the A-ring could transform the ring from a chair to a twisted conformation.
evidence: This is presented as a speculative mechanistic explanation.

claim: The two additional 1,3-diaxial interactions elicited by hopanoid 2-methylation could mimic the smoothing and/or tilting effect known for cholesterol.
source: The two additional 1,3-diaxial interactions elicited by hopanoid 2-methylation could mimic the smoothing and/or tilting effect known for cholesterol, thus rationalizing how 2-methylation may improve the ability of hopanoids to rigidify membranes (Rog et al., 2007).
evidence: This is presented as a speculative mechanistic explanation with a citation.

claim: The addition of a hydrophilic tail to form (2Me)-BHT or BHT-glucosamine may favor a stronger interaction with the outer leaflet of the OM.
source: Compared to (2Me)-Dip, the addition of a hydrophilic tail to form (2Me)-BHT or even BHT-glucosamine (Figure 1) may favor a stronger interaction with the outer leaflet of the OM, in which the lipid head group is heavily modified with hydrophilic molecules.
evidence: This is presented as a speculative explanation for the observed distribution.

claim: The relative enrichment of (2Me)-BHT in the OM is consistent with a stronger interaction with the outer leaflet of the OM.
source: The relative enrichment of (2Me)-BHT in the OM is consistent with such a scenario.
evidence: This is inferred from the quantification data.

claim: The hydrophilic tail of 2Me-BHT could affect the vertical position of the 2-methyl group in the membrane compared to 2Me-Dip.
source: The hydrophilic tail of 2Me-BHT could also affect the vertical position of the 2-methyl group in the membrane compared to 2Me-Dip (Rog et al., 2007; Poger and Mark, 2013)
evidence: This is presented as speculation with citations to prior studies.

claim: Cholesterol starts to self-organize within membranes at concentration above 10 mol%.
source: This may be due to a critical concentration needed to trigger an effect, which is consistent with molecular dynamic simulations that demonstrate cholesterol starts to self-organize within membranes at concentration above 10 mol% (Martinez-Seara et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Martinez-Seara et al., 2010.

claim: Cardiolipin significantly increases in the absence of all hopanoids.
source: In this context, it is noteworthy that cardiolipin significantly increases in the absence of all hopanoids (unpublished).
evidence: This claim is stated as unpublished data.

claim: In E. coli, cardiolipin localizes to negatively curved regions of the cell.
source: In E. coli, cardiolipin localizes to negatively curved regions of the cell (Renner and Weibel, 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Renner and Weibel, 2011.

claim: Certain hopanoid types could fulfill the geometry requirements of curved membranes and facilitate cell division or vesicle formation.
source: Looking beyond the function of methylation, it is possible that certain hopanoid types could fulfill the geometry requirements of curved membranes and facilitate cell division or vesicle formation
evidence: This is presented as speculation based on the findings.

claim: A mutant lacking the ability to transport hopanoids to the OM displays a strong cell division defect.
source: consistent with both the microdomain features observed in prior subcellular hopanoid localization studies (Doughty et al., 2014) and the strong cell division defect displayed by a mutant lacking the ability to transport hopanoids to the OM (Doughty et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Doughty et al., 2014.

claim: At higher temperature, the cell membrane became less rigid across all strains.
source: As expected, at higher temperature, the cell membrane became less rigid across all strains.
evidence: This claim is supported by whole cell membrane rigidity measurements shown in Figure 2.

claim: The lack of phenotype in the ΔhpnP strain may be due to cells synthesizing other lipids that functionally complement the absence of 2Me-hopanoids.
source: This observation reinforces the interpretation that the lack of phenotype in the ΔhpnP strain may be due to cells synthesizing other lipids that functionally complement the absence of 2Me-hopanoids, rather than due to a lack of an impact at the molecular level per se.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental results.

claim: E. coli PLE from Avanti Polar Lipids consists of 67% phosphatidylethanolamine (PE), 23.2% phosphatidylglycerol (PG), and 9.8% cardiolipin (CL) (in wt%).
source: E. coli PLE from Avanti Polar Lipids consists of 67% phosphatidylethanolamine (PE), 23.2% phosphatidylglycerol (PG), and 9.8% cardiolipin (CL) (in wt%)
evidence: This is stated as a fact about the commercial product composition.

claim: E. coli PLE has an average molecular weight identical to DOPC (786 g/mol).
source: and has an average molecular weight identical to DOPC (786 g/mol).
evidence: This is stated as a fact about the commercial product.

claim: The average molecular weight of the phospholipids without cardiolipin is 738 g/mol.
source: Nevertheless, the average molecular weight of the phospholipids without cardiolipin is 738 g/mol.
evidence: This is calculated from the LC-MS data.

claim: The discrepancy between whole cell and SUV membrane rigidity measurements could be due to the presence of lipid A and outer membrane proteins that may affect the overall membrane rigidity in whole cells.
source: This contrasts with our whole cell membrane rigidity results in which no difference in rigidity was observed (Figure 2). This discrepancy could be due to the presence of lipid A and outer membrane proteins that may affect the overall membrane rigidity in whole cells.
evidence: This is presented as a speculative explanation for the observed discrepancy.

claim: Endogenous BHT in ΔhpnP membranes may be saturating its membrane rigidifying capacity.
source: While it is possible that BHT has no effect on native membrane rigidity, given that ΔhpnP membranes contain BHT, it seems more likely that endogenous BHT is saturating its membrane rigidifying capacity, similar to what we observed for E. coli PLE (red line, Figure 6B).
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental results.

claim: The reason less 2-methylation occurs for BHT than Dip in the OM may be because less methylation of BHT is needed to significantly impact OM rigidity.
source: It is tempting to speculate that the reason less 2-methylation occurs for BHT than Dip in the OM (Figures 4, 5) is because less methylation of BHT is needed to significantly impact OM rigidity.
evidence: This is presented as speculation based on the findings.
